release.content: pubkit 0.32.0 was released on 2026-11-09 from commit 0a436c5d805f0f0d296c4ab2130644f9f056412d with these changes.

rows: CI: the reusable workflows try each setup step (make venv, npm ci, a repository's own), each hash-locked install of tests/requirements.lock and pip-audit up to three times, 15 s apart, and the managed pubkit.mk's venv target its install likewise, as pip retries no 504 and GitHub's release downloads sometimes answer one; a finding still fails pip-audit, as it fails each try. pubkit deploy walk --fulfil: a generated secret that is in Bitwarden but misshapen is planned as "replace NAME (misshapen: why)", not as generating a new one, so the typed yes knows a value goes. The dependency review leaves the owner's own reusable workflows and actions, which carry no license GitHub reads, out of its license check alone: pubkit sync lists those a repository's workflows call in .github/dependency-review-licenses.txt, of which the review takes only the owner's, and without the file it leaves out pubkit's and pubrel's; advisories still apply to them

The commands and need types that hold a secret's value, a write token or a private key are pubsec's (Sustenaut/pubsec): pubkit secrets run, app-secrets, github-app create, service-account-key create and signing-key backup now print the ./pubsec command that replaces each and exit 2, and go in the next minor; bitwarden.secret, bitwarden.generated, gcp.service-account-key, github.secret, github.variable, github.deploy-settings and k8s.secret are no longer built in. pubkit sync writes ./pubsec, which runs the pinned pubsec release, its wheel checked against its sha256, beside ./with-secrets, which now runs ./pubsec run, and lists pubsec in deploy.providers of every repository with a deploy block (sync --check fails without it); deploy-check.yml and terraform.yml run ./pubsec run. The walk asks for no write token itself: it calls each sustenaut.walk hook, prepare(ctx, plan, terminal), and pubsec's asks for it. The provider contract, the Context names a provider's types use, is frozen from this release, as the README's Provider contract section lists it: changing one is a breaking change

A wheel mirror for when GitHub's release downloads fail: pubkit.json's mirror.wheels names a base that serves each wheel at <base>/f/<sha256>/<file>.whl. The new managed tests/install-lock, which pubkit.mk's venv target and the reusable workflows' hash-locked installs now go through, tries a lock three times and then once more with each GitHub release wheel taken from the mirror, the hashes unchanged; pip-audit's last try reads the locks rewritten the same way, and ./pubkit fetches its own wheel and deploy.providers' wheels from the mirror when GitHub fails, each checked against its sha256. Without the setting, installs only retry and ./pubkit is unchanged

A provider mirror for Terraform: terraform.yml's init and the service CI's backend-less init are tried three times, 15 s apart, and then, when pubkit.json's mirror.terraform names a Terraform provider network mirror, once more with every provider from it; the module's lock still checks each archive

tests/install-lock's last try takes every package not pinned by a GitHub release URL from pubkit.json's mirror.pypi, a simple repository index (PEP 503) at <base>/simple/, instead of PyPI, the lock's hashes unchanged; the mirror block takes pypi beside wheels and terraform

The dependabot.yml pubkit sync writes no longer opens pull requests that move the owner's pubkit or pubrel pins: every github-actions entry ignores <owner>/pubkit/* and <owner>/pubrel/*, ahead of any ignores given in security.dependabot.options. Those pins move with pubkit bump, so such a pull request always failed pubkit sync --check

The merge queue skips the tests a pull request's own run already passed on the same files: job-tested, in the queue and on main, looks for a successful run of the queue's workflow (on a pull request or in the queue) whose commit has this commit's tree, following a run that skipped its tests to the run it took them from, and its coverage when not expired. pr.yml starts with tested where the queue runs it, as main.yml does; a pull request's own run, a moved main or a batch of pull requests still tests everything, and a Rust crate's queue.yml is unchanged
